title: WPSS/1091/2009 of SHANKAR SINGH Vs ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER and OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.1091/2009
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Mr. Chetan Joshi, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
 None for the respondents.
 Disciplinary proceedings were commenced
against the petitioner under Rule 14 of the
Central Civil Services (Classification, Control
and Appeal) Rules 1965. Charge-sheet was
served upon him. One Mr. S. Ganguly, Vice
Principal, K.V. No.1, Roorkee was appointed as
Enquiry Authority to look into the charges.
The Enquiry Authority submitted its report to
the disciplinary authority on 23.9.2004.
Petitioner was found guilty of the charges
framed against him. Copy of the enquiry report
was sent to the petitioner vide letter dated
17.11.2004. Petitioner was permitted to file
reply of the same within 15 days after receipt
of the order.
 Case of the petitioner, in a nutshell, is that
the copy of enquiry report was never supplied
to him, as the same was addressed to the
Principal, K.V. ITBP, Dehradun. It is, in these
circumstances, the petitioner could not file
reply to the enquiry report.
 The purpose of supplying the copy of
enquiry report to an employee is to enable him
to point out shortcomings, if any, in the
enquiry report and also the infraction of
mandatory rules. The averments made by the
petitioner that he has not received the copy of
enquiry report, has remained un-rebutted. It
should have been the endeavour of the
disciplinary authority to ensure that the copy
of enquiry report was received by the
petitioner. There was no occasion for the
petitioner not to file reply to the show cause
notice if he had received the show cause notice

with the enquiry report. Three increments of
the petitioner have been withheld with
cumulative effect by the disciplinary authority
by communication dated 12.1.2005. It is a
major penalty. Petitioner has not been
supplied with the copy of enquiry report.
There is infraction of principle of natural
justice.
 Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.
Order, under challenge, is quashed and set
aside. The disciplinary authority is directed to
supply copy of the enquiry report to the
petitioner enabling him to represent against
the same and thereafter, to proceed with the
matter in accordance with law.
 Pending application, if any, stands
disposed of as such.
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
 12.03.2018
 Rdang
